metadata.title: Nvidia, chipmakers slide premarket; Dell falls despite upbeat outlook

content.text:
Investing.com - A tech-fueled selloff that has pushed up haven demand for Treasuries appeared poised to extend into a new session on Wednesday, while reports of new U.S. tariffs on several countries further weighed on sentiment.
By 07:13 ET (12:13 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures contracts had fallen by 782 points, or 3%, S&P 500 futures had dipped by 144 points, or 2%, and Dow futures were lower by 646 points, or 1.3%.
Here's a look at some of the major premarket stock movers:
-
Nvidia fell by more than 5% before the opening bell on Wall Street, as a rally following the return of CEO Jensen Huang continued to wane. Peers Advanced Micro Devices, Intel and Broadcom were also lower.
-
Anthropic dropped by over 4%. The Claude chatbot maker ended below its initial public offering price on Tuesday, erasing what had been a sharp surge in the stock after the first-time share sale.
-
Dell Technologies declined by over 4% despite the server maker lifting its annual sales target for the third time this year.
-
AI names sank, extending a selloff in stock exposed to the nascent technology. Although AI players jumped following Huang's comeback on Monday, the euphoria has since worn off, as recent worries over the AI industry that have been prevalent in recent weeks once again took hold. Memory company Sandisk, data center power generation provider Bloom Energy, and optical technology firm Corning were all off premarket.
-
Urban Outfitters slumped after the apparel retailer posted lower-than-anticipated same store sales in the third quarter.
-
Workday also fell even after the systems software firm logged quarterly earnings and revenue that topped estimates. A restructuring charge dented third-quarter net income, however.
-
Deere & Company dropped as investors kept tabs on the company's exposure to the rapid AI infrastructure build-out.
